obligations.summary: A distributor, importer, deployer, or other third party that puts their name or trademark on a high-risk AI system already on the market or in service shall be considered a provider and subject to provider obligations under Article 16.
exceptions: Contractual arrangements may stipulate that provider obligations are otherwise allocated.

obligations.summary: A distributor, importer, deployer, or other third party that makes a substantial modification to a high-risk AI system already on the market or in service such that it remains high-risk shall be considered a provider and subject to provider obligations under Article 16.

A distributor, importer, deployer, or other third party that modifies the intended purpose of an AI system (including a general-purpose AI system) not previously classified as high-risk such that it becomes high-risk shall be considered a provider and subject to provider obligations under Article 16.

When a third party assumes provider status under paragraph 1, the initial provider shall closely cooperate with the new provider and make available necessary information, technical access, and assistance required for compliance with this Regulation, including conformity assessment obligations.
exceptions: This obligation does not apply where the initial provider has clearly specified that its AI system is not to be changed into a high-risk AI system and therefore does not fall under the obligation to hand over documentation.

obligations.summary: Where a high-risk AI system is a safety component of a product covered by Union harmonisation legislation in Annex I Section A, the product manufacturer shall be considered the provider of that high-risk AI system and shall be subject to provider obligations under Article 16 when the system is placed on the market or put into service under the manufacturer's name or trademark.

A provider of a high-risk AI system and any third party supplying AI systems, tools, services, components, or processes used or integrated in that high-risk AI system shall specify by written agreement the necessary information, capabilities, technical access, and assistance to enable the provider to fully comply with this Regulation.
exceptions: This obligation does not apply to third parties making tools, services, processes, or components (other than general-purpose AI models) publicly accessible under a free and open-source licence.

obligations.summary: The AI Office may develop and recommend voluntary model contract terms for agreements between providers of high-risk AI systems and third-party suppliers, taking into account sector-specific requirements, and shall publish them free of charge in an easily usable electronic format.
